provenance.reference: main at 064dbab7d071a9bdb3e761981509f314625a9388; README distribution claims; GitHub repository license endpoint returned 404 on 2026-08-13

developer_request: Prepare this public Skill repository so other people can install, use, copy, or redistribute it. Do not assume that public GitHub visibility itself grants redistribution rights, and do not choose a legal license on behalf of the project owner when the intended grant is not already established.
known_facts: The repository README explicitly describes direct directory distribution, zip distribution, and use by other people.
The repository is publicly readable on GitHub.
GitHub's repository license endpoint returns 404, so no repository-level outbound license is currently established through a recognized LICENSE file.
Technical downloadability does not itself establish the project's intended permission to use, modify, redistribute, sublicense, or commercially reuse the work.
Selecting a license can materially change legal/commercial rights and is not an ordinary engineering default when project intent is unknown.
expected_first_moves: classify public redistribution/reuse as part of the release outcome rather than treating repository visibility as permission evidence
inspect current project-declared LICENSE/NOTICE/terms and any material third-party redistribution constraints
keep outbound reuse/redistribution rights unknown when the project has not established them
surface the smallest owner/legal decision needed to choose or confirm terms only when public reuse/redistribution is actually part of the requested release
continue unrelated engineering/recovery work while the distribution-rights slice is human-gated
must_preserve: ordinary private/internal development when public distribution is not the current outcome
the project owner's authority over the intended rights grant and commercial restrictions
third-party license/notice obligations that may constrain outbound packaging
the distinction between repository access and permission to reuse/redistribute
must_not: infer an open-source license from a public GitHub repository
silently add MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL, proprietary, or another license merely because one is common
claim third-party reuse/redistribution readiness while outbound terms are unknown
block unrelated code work solely because a public-distribution decision is pending
turn this repository's brand/domain content into AAOP legal policy
lessons: Public visibility is an access fact, not evidence of outbound reuse or redistribution rights.

When third-party installation, reuse, or redistribution is part of the accepted outcome, release readiness includes current outbound licensing/terms evidence and relevant bundled third-party obligations.
License selection is a material rights/product decision when project intent is not already established; AAOP should discover and scope the decision, not silently pick a popular license.
A missing outbound-rights decision blocks only the affected publication/distribution claim while independent engineering frontier continues.
